slot.brief: A radioactive sample has a given half-life; ask for the fraction/mass remaining after a specified number of half-lives (simple counting).

stem: A radioactive substance has a half-life of 15 days. After 60 days, its mass is found to be 0.5 g. The initial mass of the substance was:

verdicts.working: 60 days is 4 half-lives, so the remaining mass is the initial mass divided by 2^4. Initial mass = 0.5 × 16 = 8 g.

working:
Number of half-lives: n = 60 / 15 = 4. Fraction remaining = (1/2)^4 = 1/16. Let m0 be initial mass. Then m0 × (1/16) = 0.5 g, so m0 = 0.5 × 16 = 8 g.

Independent check: 60 days is 4 half-lives, so the remaining mass is the initial mass divided by 2^4. Initial mass = 0.5 × 16 = 8 g.
solution:
Number of half-lives in $60$ days: $n=60/15=4$.
$$0.5=m_0\left(\frac12\right)^4\quad\Rightarrow\quad m_0=0.5\times16=8\text{ g}.$$
